newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon urges U.S. to lift travel ban.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon urges U.S. to lift travel ban.

text.p: Lebanese President Elias Hrawi urged the United States on Monday to end a ban on Americans travelling to the Middle Eastern country.
Washington imposed the ban in 1985 after Moslem militants hijacked a TWA airliner to Beirut and killed an American passenger.

In his annual address to foreign diplomats, Hrawi thanked Washington for hosting a "Friends of Lebanon" conference of donor nations last month but said the United States should lift the travel ban to show its support for post-civil war Lebanon.

"As we thank the United States for sponsoring this meeting, we await its undertaking to lift the ban on the travel of Americans to Lebanon to substantiate this sponsorship, its dimensions and to stress its support to Lebanon," Hrawi said.

U.S. President Bill Clinton said on December 16 while the Washington meeting was in progress that he was maintaining the ban since his advisers did not think it was safe for American businessmen to travel to Lebanon at present.
Lebanon, which has been pressing hard for the ban to be lifted, suspects that Washington is using it as a bargaining chip to force it to sign a peace treaty with Israel.
Hrawi also urged friendly nations to help Lebanon rebuild after the 1975-90 civil war. International donors at the Washington meeting pledged more than $3.2 billion in aid.
